# 2 Kings Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 233r–233v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_012_page_001.jpg, 2KI_012_page_002.jpg

---

**12:1** In-the-seventh year of-Yehu, Yo'ash began-to-reign [malakh], and-forty years he-reigned in-Yerushalayim. And-the-name of-his-mother [was] Tsivyah from-Be'er-Sheva.

**12:2** And-did Yo'ash the-right [ha-yashar] in-the-eyes of-YHWH all his-days, [in] which Yehoyada the-priest instructed-him [horahu].

**12:3** Only the-high-places [ha-bamot] were-not removed [lo saru]; the-people [were] still sacrificing [mezabbechim] and-burning-incense [meqatterim] on-the-high-places.

**12:4** And-said Yo'ash to the-priests: All the-silver of-the-holy-things [kesef ha-qodashim] that is-brought [to] the-house of-YHWH — silver of-a-person-passing [kesef 'over], each the-silver of-the-souls of-his-valuation ['erkho], all silver that comes-up upon the-heart [lev] of-a-man to-bring [to] the-house of-YHWH —

**12:5** let-the-priests take [yiqchu] for-themselves, each from his-acquaintance [makkaro], and-they shall-repair [yechazequ] the-breach [bedeq] of-the-house, wherever a-breach [bedeq] is-found there.

**12:6** And-it-was in-the-twenty-third year of-King Yo'ash, the-priests had-not repaired [lo chizzequ] the-breach of-the-house.

**12:7** And-called King Yo'ash Yehoyada the-priest and-the-priests, and-said to-them: Why are-you-not repairing [mechazeqim] the-breach of-the-house? And-now, do-not take silver from-your-acquaintances, but for-the-breach of-the-house give-it [titenuhu].

**12:8** And-agreed [vayye'otu] the-priests not to-take silver from the-people and-not to-repair the-breach of-the-house.

**12:9** And-took Yehoyada the-priest a-chest ['aron echad] and-bored [vayiqqov] a-hole [chor] in-its-lid [dalto], and-set [vayitten] it beside the-altar, on-the-right [as] a-man comes to-the-house of-YHWH. And-put there the-priests, keepers of-the-threshold [shomerey ha-saf], all the-silver that-was-brought [to] the-house of-YHWH.

**12:10** And-it-was when-they-saw that [there was] much [rav] silver in-the-chest, and-came-up the-scribe [sofer] of-the-king and-the-high [ha-gadol] priest, and-they-bound-up [vayatsuru] and-counted [vayimnu] the-silver that-was-found [in] the-house of-YHWH.

**12:11** And-they-gave the-silver that-was-weighed [ha-metuqqan] into the-hands of-the-doers of-the-work [osey ha-melakhah], the-appointed-ones [ha-mufqadim] [over] the-house of-YHWH. And-they-brought-it-out [vayotsi'uhu] to-the-craftsmen of-wood [charshe ha-'ets] and-to-the-builders [la-bonim] who-worked [on] the-house of-YHWH,

**12:12** and-to-the-masons [la-goderim] and-to-the-hewers of-stone [le-chotsevey ha-even], and-to-buy timber ['etsim] and-hewn stone [avney machtsev] to-repair the-breach of-the-house of-YHWH, and-for-all that-went-out upon the-house to-repair-it [le-chazqah].

**12:13** However, there-were-not made for-the-house of-YHWH basins of-silver [sippot kesef], snuffers [mezammerot], bowls [mizraqot], trumpets [chatsotsrot] — any vessel [keli] of-gold or-vessel of-silver — from-the-silver that-was-brought [to] the-house of-YHWH.

**12:14** For to-the-doers of-the-work they-gave it, and-they-repaired [ve-chizzequ] with-it the-house of-YHWH.

**12:15** And-they-did-not reckon [lo yechassevu] with the-men into whose-hand they-gave the-silver to-give to-the-doers of-the-work, for in-faithfulness ['emunah] they were-doing [osim].

**12:16** Silver of-guilt-offering [kesef asham] and-silver of-sin-offering [kesef chatta'ot] was-not brought [to] the-house of-YHWH; to-the-priests it belonged [la-kohanim yihyu].

**12:17** Then went-up Chaza'el [Hazael] king of-Aram and-fought against Gat and-captured-it [vayilkedah]. And-set Chaza'el his-face [panav] to-go-up against Yerushalayim.

**12:18** And-took Yo'ash king of-Yehudah all the-holy-things [ha-qodashim] that Yehoshafat and-Yehoram and-Achazyahu his-fathers, kings of-Yehudah, had-consecrated [hiqdiyshu], and-his-own holy-things, and-all the-gold that-was-found in-the-treasuries [be-otsrot] of-the-house of-YHWH and-the-house of-the-king, and-sent [them] to-Chaza'el king of-Aram. And-he-went-up from-upon Yerushalayim.

**12:19** And-the-rest of-the-acts [divrey] of-Yo'ash and-all that he-did, are-they-not written in-the-book of-the-chronicles [sefer divrey ha-yamim] of-the-kings of-Yehudah?

**12:20** And-arose his-servants and-bound a-conspiracy [qesher], and-struck Yo'ash [at] the-house of-Millo' [beyt millo'], [on] the-descent [ha-yored] of-Silla'.

**12:21** And-Yozakhar [Jozachar] son of-Shim'at and-Yehozavad [Jehozabad] son of-Shomer, his-servants, struck-him and-he-died. And-they-buried-him with-his-fathers in-the-city of-David. And-reigned Amatsyah [Amaziah] his-son in-his-place.

**12:22** [Note: In many English versions, 12:1 Hebrew = 11:21 English, with the verse numbering offset by one throughout this chapter. EMET follows the Hebrew (MT) verse numbering.]

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — Hebrew verse numbering:** The Hebrew text of 2 Kings 12 begins with what many English versions number as 11:21 (the accession notice for Joash). Throughout this chapter, the Hebrew numbering runs one verse ahead of the standard English numbering. EMET follows the Masoretic numbering.

**v.5 — from his acquaintance (makkaro):** Each priest was to collect silver from people known to him — a personal, decentralized system. The word *makkar* suggests a familiar relationship, possibly a regular donor or commercial contact.

**v.9 — the chest:** Jehoiada's innovation — a collection box with a hole bored in the lid — is one of the earliest recorded instances of institutionalized fundraising. It replaces the failed system of priestly collection with transparent, centralized giving.

**v.15 — in faithfulness:** The administrators of the temple repair fund are not audited because they act *be-emunah* (in faithfulness/integrity). This remarkable statement of institutional trust contrasts sharply with the priests who failed to use collected funds properly.

**v.18 — Joash buys off Hazael:** The same king who restored the temple now empties it. The irony is structural: the chapter begins with temple restoration and ends with temple depletion, framing Joash's reign as ultimately tragic.

*— EMET*
